headline_marked: [[AMD Mustang Peak]] Threadripper CPUs to feature 144 cores, DDR5, PCIe 6.0
headline: AMD Mustang Peak Threadripper CPUs to feature 144 cores, DDR5, PCIe 6.0
summary: AMD's next-gen Threadripper processors, codenamed 'Mustang Peak,' are set to debut with up to 144 cores, DDR5 memory, and PCIe 6.0 support on a new TR6 socket.
details: The first official details for AMD's upcoming 'Mustang Peak' Threadripper CPUs have emerged, confirming key specifications for the Zen 6-based processors. These chips will utilize TSMC's 2nm-class process for their Core Complex Dies (CCDs).

Key confirmed features include support for DDR5 memory and PCI Express 6.0, necessitating a new platform codenamed 'TR6' for installation. This upgrade promises significant improvements in data transfer speeds and memory bandwidth.

The 'Mustang Peak' processors are expected to feature 'Powderhorn' CCDs, increasing the core count per chiplet from 8 to 12. This could push the maximum core count on Threadripper Pro CPUs to a staggering 144 cores, up from the current 96.

Zen 6 is also anticipated to push clock rates significantly above 6 GHz, potentially leading to substantial performance gains. To feed these high-clocked cores, AMD may increase memory channels, possibly adopting the 16-channel configuration seen in EPYC 'Venice' processors.

With 144 cores and advanced memory bandwidth capabilities, these processors are positioned for extreme workloads. PCIe 6.0 will offer up to 256 GB/second bidirectional bandwidth on a x16 link, ensuring ample connectivity for high-performance devices.
AMD's 'Mustang Peak' Threadripper CPUs are expected to launch in mid-to-late 2027, marking a significant leap in processing power for high-end workstations and servers.
